hero.headline: Port St. Lucie SWAT raid uncovers cocaine, meth, gun in home with infant
hero.teaser: A Port St. Lucie SWAT team served a search warrant at a Fields Avenue home following an undercover cocaine buy, finding drugs, a firearm, and stolen identification documents in a residence where an infant was present.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested Bruce Alexander Francis, 30, after a SWAT team search warrant execution at 406 SW Fields Ave. uncovered suspected cocaine, methamphetamine, marijuana, a revolver, ammunition, stolen identification documents, and cash in a home where an infant lived.

 SWAT officers served the warrant about 5:30 a.m. on September 22. Francis and five other people exited the home. Officers reported seeing Francis run from the bedroom to the bathroom and throw something before closing the door. Detectives found suspected cocaine in the master bedroom and bathroom, including bags in and around a toilet.

 Police used a confidential informant earlier in September to buy about 3.5 grams of cocaine from Francis at the home. The substance tested presumptively positive for cocaine and weighed about 4 grams. Francis told detectives that any drugs in the home belonged to him but declined to provide further information. He denied having a phone, though investigators said they found the cellphone allegedly used in the cocaine transaction.

 A woman told police she shared the master bedroom with Francis and a baby. She said Francis stayed home with the children during the day and that she did not know what he did for work. Police found a Fanta bottle containing a green liquid in the refrigerator that tested presumptively positive for methamphetamine. The liquid weighed about 180.5 grams.

 The search turned up $2,560 in cash, a .22-caliber revolver, .22-caliber and 9mm ammunition, scales, plastic baggies, suspected marijuana, and THC products. In the master bedroom closet and elsewhere in the home, police found driver's licenses, Social Security cards, debit cards, and credit cards belonging to several other people. The documents belonged to people in Texas and Florida.

 Francis was charged with trafficking in methamphetamine, possession of cocaine with intent to sell, marijuana possession, possession of drug equipment, three counts of possessing another person's identification without consent, evidence tampering, and two counts of possession of a weapon or ammunition by a convicted felon. He was also charged with selling cocaine and using a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony in the earlier cocaine sale case.

 Police said Francis had a 2014 felony conviction. His bond was set at $530,000 on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Florida to begin issuing redesigned driver licenses and ID cards
cards.teaser: Florida will begin issuing newly redesigned driver licenses and identification cards Sept. 30, featuring updated security elements and imagery tied to the state's history.
cards.body:
Florida will begin issuing newly redesigned driver licenses and identification cards on Wednesday, Sept. 30, with the updated credentials becoming available at service centers statewide.

 Gov. Ron DeSantis announced the rollout Tuesday during a Florida Cabinet meeting at the state Capitol. The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles said online orders for the new credentials are expected to become available through MyDMVPortal by early November.

 The redesigned cards include updated security features along with imagery highlighting Florida history and landmarks.

 The front of the card features Castillo de San Marcos in St. Augustine as its background image. Florida's orange is incorporated into the lettering of the state name, while a manatee appears in the lower left corner. An alligator is incorporated into the REAL ID star in the upper right corner.

 The back of the card features Space Shuttle Discovery, recognizing Florida's Space Coast. Discovery flew 39 missions before making its final landing in Florida in 2011. The credential also includes the phrase “Let Us Alone,” which appeared on Florida's first unofficial state flag.

 FLHSMV Executive Director Dave Kerner said the redesign builds on previous efforts to strengthen fraud protection and identity verification while maintaining compliance with federal REAL ID requirements.

 The updated credentials will also include a “Temporary Non-Domiciled” marking for certain commercial driver licenses and commercial learner's permits.

 Florida residents do not need to replace a currently valid driver license or identification card simply because of the redesign. Existing credentials will remain valid until they expire and will be phased out over time.

 Additional information about the new design is available at https://www.flhsmv.gov/driver-licenses-id-cards/newdl/. Online credential services are available at https://mydmvportal.flhsmv.gov/.

cards.headline: Florida to begin issuing redesigned driver licenses and ID cards
cards.teaser: Florida will begin issuing newly redesigned driver licenses and identification cards Sept. 30, featuring updated security elements and imagery tied to the state's history.
cards.body:
Florida will begin issuing newly redesigned driver licenses and identification cards on Wednesday, Sept. 30, with the updated credentials becoming available at service centers statewide.

 Gov. Ron DeSantis announced the rollout Tuesday during a Florida Cabinet meeting at the state Capitol. The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles said online orders for the new credentials are expected to become available through MyDMVPortal by early November.

 The redesigned cards include updated security features along with imagery highlighting Florida history and landmarks.

 The front of the card features Castillo de San Marcos in St. Augustine as its background image. Florida's orange is incorporated into the lettering of the state name, while a manatee appears in the lower left corner. An alligator is incorporated into the REAL ID star in the upper right corner.

 The back of the card features Space Shuttle Discovery, recognizing Florida's Space Coast. Discovery flew 39 missions before making its final landing in Florida in 2011. The credential also includes the phrase “Let Us Alone,” which appeared on Florida's first unofficial state flag.

 FLHSMV Executive Director Dave Kerner said the redesign builds on previous efforts to strengthen fraud protection and identity verification while maintaining compliance with federal REAL ID requirements.

 The updated credentials will also include a “Temporary Non-Domiciled” marking for certain commercial driver licenses and commercial learner's permits.

 Florida residents do not need to replace a currently valid driver license or identification card simply because of the redesign. Existing credentials will remain valid until they expire and will be phased out over time.

 Additional information about the new design is available at https://www.flhsmv.gov/driver-licenses-id-cards/newdl/. Online credential services are available at https://mydmvportal.flhsmv.gov/.
